**Method 1**

When we add a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always twice the real part of the complex number.

For the given complex number $z=6-10\text{i},$ the real part is $Re(z)=6,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z+\overset{―}{z} & =2\text{Re}(z) \\  & =2(6) \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of adding the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=6-10\text{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overset{―}{z}=6+10\text{i}.$

Adding, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z+\overset{―}{z} & =(6-10\text{i})+(6+10\text{i}) \\  & =(6+6)+\text{i}(-10+10) \\  & =12+\text{i}0 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
